newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ share prices end weaker, off session low.
newsitem.headline: NZ share prices end weaker, off session low.

text.p: * NZ share prices end weaker but off session low
* Leading stocks all ease on light turnover
* Lion Nathan edges back slightly but talk remains
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index -15.85 at 2,558.78

New Zealand share prices ended weaker but off their low for the session on light turnover following a weak close on Wall Street on Friday.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index lost 15.85 points to close at 2,558.78 after sinking at one point to 2,553.774.
Turnover, worth NZ$40 million, was typically low for a Monday but also reflected the effects of a bank holiday in Australia.
Campbell Stuart at SBC Warburg said there would be interest in Wednesday's jobs data, particularly if a weak number leads to a further easing of conditions by the Reserve Bank.
But he expected overseas equity markets, particuarly in the U.S., to be the key determinant for direction in the short term.
All leaders were weaker but Carter Holt Harvey managed a partial recovery, closing three cents down at NZ$3.79, having dropped at one point to $3.75.
Lion Nathan edged two cents down to NZ$4.10 but was still not far from its three-and-a-half year high set last week.
Brokers were still largely in the dark as to why the stock had performed so strongly.
Possible explanations have ranged between talk of corporate forays into Lion to an improvement in the brewer's market share position.
Fletcher Forest attracted high turnvoer, with stock worth NZ$5.16 million trading. Forests ended two cents down at NZ$1.99.
In the minor oil explorers, Amity Oil shot up 25 cents to NZ$1.40 after some favourable news coverage about its Australian prospects over the weekend.
Chemicals ground Fernz Corp, which reported its final result last week, lost seven cents to NZ$5.25.
